academics.1: Student. You know that 1066 is more than a Beverly Hills area code.
academics.2: College. You can quote the classics, recognize major cultural movements, and tell Ming from Mogul.
academics.3: Masters. You could write a journal article.
academics.5: Scholar. Scholars worldwide recognize you as one of the foremost experts of your time.
academics.6: Luminary. Your corrections to the canon become the canon while you are still around to see it.
academics.7: Authority. Specialists arrive to argue and leave quoting you.
academics.8: Canon. You hold in your head a stratum a department would need a library for.
academics.9: Keeper. The past is a working tool, not a reference: you can see how an argument ends because you have already watched it.
academics.10: Wellspring. If a thread of humane learning snapped somewhere, you still have the end of it.

alertness.1: Novice. You are not a mindless drone.
alertness.3: Competent. You keep a sharp eye on your surroundings.
alertness.4: Expert. Whether from paranoia or good sense, you are rarely surprised.
alertness.5: Master. Your senses are on par with a wild animal's.
alertness.6: Legend. You catch a lie in someone's posture before you catch it in their words.
alertness.7: Marvel. An ambush that would take a hunter is already noise to you.
alertness.8: Myth. You feel a stare through a wall and a crowd.
alertness.9: Byword. Even an elder who is used to being a shadow still leaves you a trace.
alertness.10: Absolute. If something in the night moved, you already know what.

animalKen.1: Novice. A domesticated horse will let you pet it.
animalKen.2: Practiced. You can raise a puppy.
animalKen.3: Competent. You can train a guard dog.
animalKen.5: Master. You can tame animals without supernatural powers.
animalKen.6: Legend. A wild beast accepts your will without training and without fear.
animalKen.7: Marvel. A pack, a stable, or a swarm of rats acts as an extension of your hand.
animalKen.8: Myth. You read a beast more truly than a hunter reads a track.
animalKen.9: Byword. An animal that will not suffer people comes to you on its own.
animalKen.10: Absolute. There is no command between you and the beast. There is an understanding that does not need a language.

archery.1: Novice. You hit a target if it is large and standing still.
archery.2: Practiced. A hunting distance is familiar.
archery.3: Competent. You take a beast or a person before they are truly running.
archery.4: Expert. A moving target is a choice, not luck.
archery.5: Master. You loose as if the arrow already knew the way.
archery.6: Legend. Wind and bad light barely spoil the shot.
archery.7: Marvel. You drop a target others are still trying to find.
archery.8: Myth. You meet a volley that should have covered you with a shaft of your own.
archery.9: Byword. They say you can thread a visor-slit from the saddle.
archery.10: Absolute. The bow is a look with a shaft. Distance is only a courtesy.

athletics.1: Novice. You had an active childhood.
athletics.4: Expert. A favorite in your sport.
athletics.6: Legend. Mortal records are a warm-up for you, not a ceiling.
athletics.7: Marvel. You take heights and distances a human body was not built for.
athletics.8: Myth. A wall, a roof, and a drop are the rest of the step, not an obstacle.
athletics.9: Byword. They tell of you as the one who outran a horse and did not lose breath.
athletics.10: Absolute. Flesh obeys you as if weight were a courtesy, not a law.

brawl.1: Novice. You fought as a child.
brawl.2: Practiced. You have been in a few fights.
brawl.3: Competent. You fight regularly and hard, and you usually leave in better shape than your opponents.
brawl.4: Expert. You could be a serious contender in the boxing ring.
brawl.5: Master. You can kill three men in four seconds.
brawl.6: Legend. A seasoned fighter is one exchange for you.
brawl.7: Marvel. You break a guard before the other person understands that the fight has started.
brawl.8: Myth. Several enemies are a queue, not a numerical advantage.
brawl.9: Byword. People know you by how quickly a room goes quiet.
brawl.10: Absolute. Your hands are a weapon that needs neither a blade nor a name for the blow.

commerce.1: Novice. You do not give away the last coin for the first price named.
commerce.2: Practiced. You can read a market: where they lie, and where you can haggle.
commerce.3: Competent. You run a trade and stay ahead.
commerce.4: Expert. A caravan, a shop, or a toll rests on your accounting.
commerce.5: Master. You make a fortune on a difference other people do not notice.
commerce.6: Legend. A foreign good and a foreign city do not stop you naming the true price.
commerce.7: Marvel. You ruin a rival with a deal that looks profitable to him.
commerce.8: Myth. Coin, debt, and rumor of goods gather where you stand.
commerce.9: Byword. A trade route changes course if you decide it should.
commerce.10: Absolute. The market is a conversation. You speak last.

computer.1: Student. You know where to click.
computer.2: College. You can handle information on a computer with ease.
computer.4: Doctorate. You can make good money as a consultant.
computer.5: Scholar. You are the undisputed master of your craft.
computer.6: Luminary. Other people's systems are rooms with an unlocked door. The door is just not where they drew it.
computer.7: Authority. You write what other people later write on, and you keep a back door.
computer.8: Canon. The network, the hardware, and someone else's code answer you faster than their owners do.
computer.9: Keeper. A machine you have never seen still tells you how it is built.
computer.10: Wellspring. There is no closed system for you. There is a system that has not confessed yet.

crafts.1: Novice. You did wood shop in high school.
crafts.2: Practiced. You have started developing your own style.
crafts.4: Expert. Your work could be shown in a college textbook.
crafts.5: Master. You have practically no equal in your field.
crafts.6: Legend. A thing of yours outlives the fashion and reaches hands that know a master's hand.
crafts.7: Marvel. You repair and make what other people lack both the tool and the concept for.
crafts.8: Myth. The material obeys you as if it remembered the shape in advance.
crafts.9: Byword. Craftsmen argue about how you did it, and they do not agree.
crafts.10: Absolute. In your craft there is no model left. You are the model.

dodge.1: Novice. You can duck your head into your shoulders by reflex.
dodge.2: Practiced. You finished a self-defense course.
dodge.3: Competent. You can dodge a thrown rock, maybe even a knife.
dodge.4: Expert. Even a skilled fighter has trouble hitting you.
dodge.5: Master. You can almost dodge bullets in the open.
dodge.6: Legend. You leave the line even when the blow already seems to have landed.
dodge.7: Marvel. A burst, a knife from a crowd, a car: you choose which of them will not happen.
dodge.8: Myth. Hitting you in the open is nearly an insult to the shooter.
dodge.9: Byword. They say the bullet asks permission.
dodge.10: Absolute. You are not faster than the shot. You are simply already not where they aimed.

drive.1: Novice. You know how an automatic transmission works.
drive.2: Practiced. You can drive a stick.
drive.4: Expert. NASCAR racer or tank driver.
drive.5: Master. You can pull James Bond stunts behind the wheel.
drive.6: Legend. A car is a body to you: the skid, the brake, and the gap in traffic are feel.
drive.7: Marvel. You get the living off a speed where other people are already a wreck.
drive.8: Myth. A tank, a rig, or a strange machine is a question of a minute, not of training.
drive.9: Byword. A chase ends where you decide it ends.
drive.10: Absolute. Road, metal, and speed obey you as if that had been the plan.

empathy.1: Novice. You sometimes let someone cry on your shoulder.
empathy.2: Practiced. Sometimes you can literally feel another person's pain.
empathy.3: Competent. You can see what motivates other people.
empathy.4: Expert. It is almost impossible to lie to you.
empathy.5: Master. The human soul holds no mysteries for you.
empathy.6: Legend. You hear a feeling the person has not named to themselves yet.
empathy.7: Marvel. Mask, nature, and a lie are three different voices in one sentence to you.
empathy.8: Myth. You can name someone else's pain more exactly than its owner can.
empathy.9: Byword. The soul across from you is an open book, margins already marked.
empathy.10: Absolute. You cannot be fooled by a feeling. You can only be confessed to.

etiquette.1: Novice. You know when to keep your mouth shut.
etiquette.2: Practiced. You have been to a formal event or two.
etiquette.3: Competent. You even know which piece of silver to use.
etiquette.4: Expert. Her Majesty would be impressed by your charm.
etiquette.5: Master. If the right people come to dinner, you can stop a war — or start one.
etiquette.6: Legend. You do not err in a foreign court, even if no one explained the protocol.
etiquette.7: Marvel. Insult and peace differ by one word in your phrasing, and you know the word.
etiquette.8: Myth. Princes and mortal powers take your tone for their own custom.
etiquette.9: Byword. A war that can be started at table does not start in your presence without your consent.
etiquette.10: Absolute. Any society is your table. You decide who belongs at it.

expression.1: Novice. Your talent is limited to crude poetry or notes in a notebook.
expression.2: Practiced. You could lead a college debate team.
expression.3: Competent. You could be a successful writer.
expression.4: Expert. Your work is worthy of a Pulitzer.
expression.5: Master. A talent like yours comes once in a generation.
expression.6: Legend. Your sentence outlives the evening and becomes someone else's quotation.
expression.7: Marvel. You move a room's mood with one line, even when you are lying.
expression.8: Myth. What you wrote or said changes what people believe.
expression.9: Byword. A generation speaks in your phrasing and thinks it arrived there alone.
expression.10: Absolute. A word in your mouth is already an act no one can wave off.

finance.1: Student. You have had a few business lessons.
finance.2: College. You have some experience and can keep your own finances in order.
finance.3: Masters. You could be a successful broker.
finance.4: Doctorate. Entire corporations follow your financial advice.
finance.5: Scholar. You can get rich with a $20 check.
finance.6: Luminary. Markets and other people's books are a mood to you, and you know how to spoil one on purpose.
finance.7: Authority. A fortune other people spend decades gathering, you assemble in the course of a deal.
finance.8: Canon. Corporations and underground tills are equally transparent when you need the figures.
finance.9: Keeper. You can bring a house down or raise it up so that people will call it an accident.
finance.10: Wellspring. Money comes where you look, and leaves the people you point at.

firearms.1: Novice. You shot a BB gun as a child.
firearms.2: Practiced. You sometimes spend a few hours at a shooting club.
firearms.3: Competent. You have survived a firefight or two.
firearms.4: Expert. You can hit a man on the move.
firearms.5: Master. You have been practicing since they invented the Winchester.
firearms.6: Legend. A moving target, bad light, and a strange gun barely change the result.
firearms.7: Marvel. You shoot as if a burst were one intention, not several shots.
firearms.8: Myth. A weapon you are seeing for the first time does not jam in your hands and does not lie.
firearms.9: Byword. They say you hit where you look, and that is no longer a metaphor.
firearms.10: Absolute. The barrel is the rest of the gaze. Distance is a detail.

hearthWisdom.1: Novice. You know which herb stays out of the pot, and which omen you do not argue with aloud.
hearthWisdom.2: Practiced. A village recognizes you as someone who knows how things are done.
hearthWisdom.3: Competent. You treat simple hurts, read the weather, and remember which bloodline feuds with which.
hearthWisdom.4: Expert. The old come to ask you what never gets written down.
hearthWisdom.5: Master. The spoken knowledge of the district lives with you, not in one house.
hearthWisdom.6: Legend. A strange country gives you its signs in a few nights.
hearthWisdom.7: Marvel. You can tell a grandmother's tale from a warning that still works.
hearthWisdom.8: Myth. Herb, omen, and local fear are one study to you.
hearthWisdom.9: Byword. They send for you when the book is silent and the matter is already burning.
hearthWisdom.10: Absolute. Folk memory speaks in your voice, and it is rarely wrong.

intimidation.4: Expert. The force of your authority hangs in the air and frightens passersby.
intimidation.5: Master. You can frighten wild animals.
intimidation.6: Legend. You do not need to raise your voice. The room gets quieter on its own.
intimidation.7: Marvel. Armed people look for a reason not to anger you.
intimidation.8: Myth. The Beast in someone else recognizes an elder in you and steps back.
intimidation.9: Byword. A threat you never spoke still gets carried out.
intimidation.10: Absolute. Your attention is already a punishment. The wild and the dead understand that.

investigation.1: Student. You have read a few Agatha Christie novels.
investigation.6: Luminary. A clue the scene did not want to give up still ends up in your hands.
investigation.7: Authority. You rebuild a night from dust, a pause, and what is not at the scene.
investigation.8: Canon. You tell a false trail from a true one before anyone has spent time on it.
investigation.9: Keeper. A crime everyone called closed opens itself when you are there.
investigation.10: Wellspring. If it happened, you can say how, even after everyone has already lied.

law.1: Student. You have watched a few courtroom dramas.
law.2: College. You are in law school, or you have already passed the exams.
law.3: Masters. You can file a competent brief.
law.4: Doctorate. A lot of powerful people have your number.
law.5: Scholar. You could find a loophole in a contract with the devil.
law.6: Luminary. You find a gap in a law that was written against gaps like that.
law.7: Authority. Court, tradition, and contract are one text to you, and you know which line is lying.
law.8: Canon. Powerful people call you before they make the mistake, and sometimes after.
law.9: Keeper. You can turn guilt into procedure, and procedure into a rescue.
law.10: Wellspring. Even an oath everyone called unbreakable has an exit in your reading.

leadership.1: Novice. Captain of your little-league team.
leadership.5: Master. You could be lord and master of a whole nation.
leadership.6: Legend. People follow you when it does not profit them, and they call it their own decision.
leadership.7: Marvel. You gather other wills into one order without shouting.
leadership.8: Myth. A city or a court holds its line while you are looking that way.
leadership.9: Byword. Your silence is read as policy, and it is carried out.
leadership.10: Absolute. You can turn the night of a whole people, if you decide it is necessary.

legerdemain.1: Novice. A coin vanishes if the audience is not really looking.
legerdemain.2: Practiced. You lift a purse from someone standing side-on.
legerdemain.3: Competent. Your hands work while you hold their eyes.
legerdemain.4: Expert. A search and someone else's pocket are nearly the same job.
legerdemain.5: Master. An object changes owners, and the new owner thinks it was theirs for another minute.
legerdemain.6: Legend. You steal from the person who is waiting to be robbed.
legerdemain.7: Marvel. A knot, a seal, or a closed fist does not keep you from taking what you came for.
legerdemain.8: Myth. The thing disappears out of hands that were gripping it.
legerdemain.9: Byword. They do not tell stories about you. They tell stories about an empty purse.
legerdemain.10: Absolute. If hands can carry it, it is already half yours.

linguistics.8: Canon. One hundred and twenty-eight additional languages, dead ones included.
linguistics.9: Keeper. Two hundred and fifty-six additional languages. An accent is a lexicon to you.
linguistics.10: Wellspring. Five hundred and twelve additional languages. Speech is one family to you.

medicine.1: Student. You have finished a first-aid course.
medicine.5: Scholar. The world medical community considers you a modern Asclepius.
medicine.6: Luminary. A body is a diagram to you: you repair what other people write off.
medicine.7: Authority. You can still put the rare, the foreign, and the nearly dead back to work.
medicine.8: Canon. Your diagnosis arrives ahead of the symptoms the patient has noticed.
medicine.9: Keeper. What medicine calls a miracle, you call a Tuesday.
medicine.10: Wellspring. Living flesh obeys your understanding as if you had been present when it was arranged.

melee.1: Novice. You know which end of a knife to hold.
melee.2: Practiced. You have been in a couple of street fights.
melee.3: Competent. You could captain a college fencing team.
melee.4: Expert. You could keep order at the prince's court.
melee.5: Master. Your enemies would rather face a SWAT team than your blade.
melee.6: Legend. A blade, a stake, and a club in your hand are the same conversation.
melee.7: Marvel. You hold a court or an alley against people who are better armed.
melee.8: Myth. Disarming you is harder than beating you with a weapon.
melee.9: Byword. Your blow is recognized by the defense that was late before the swing.
melee.10: Absolute. Steel obeys you as if it remembered whom you have already killed.

occult.1: Student. You have read a few books about the New Age.
occult.2: College. There seems to be some truth in the rumors you have heard.
occult.3: Masters. You have heard a great deal and seen little.
occult.4: Doctorate. You can spot an outright lie and draw a conclusion about the rest.
occult.5: Scholar. You know most of the major truths of the hidden world.
occult.6: Luminary. You separate heresy from a working ritual, and you know which lie still kills.
occult.7: Authority. The hidden world has a map for you, blank spots included, and you know how to go around them.
occult.8: Canon. You hold the names, bans, and prices of the night as if you had signed them yourself.
occult.9: Keeper. What other people call a myth, you can check, and most of the time you already have.
occult.10: Wellspring. The major truths of the hidden world are not merely known to you. You use them.

performance.1: Novice. You could sing in a church choir.
performance.2: Practiced. You could play a lead in a college production.
performance.3: Competent. You are in demand at every local club.
performance.4: Expert. You have the talent to become a national sensation.
performance.5: Master. You are a virtuoso without equal.
performance.6: Legend. The hall is yours from the first note, even if no one knows the name yet.
performance.7: Marvel. You lead someone else's feeling where you need it, and they call that art.
performance.8: Myth. People who were not in the hall tell the story of the performance.
performance.9: Byword. Virtuosity is a habit for you, not a peak.
performance.10: Absolute. While you play, the truth of the room is the one you chose.

politics.2: College. A member of a political party.
politics.3: Masters. Campaign manager or a host on the radio.
politics.5: Scholar. You could be chosen the next President of the United States.
politics.6: Luminary. You move a decision before it has reached the agenda.
politics.7: Authority. A city, a sect, or a party treats your position as its own necessity.
politics.8: Canon. Power comes to consult you even when it pretends it does not.
politics.9: Keeper. You can seat a figure or remove one so that people will call it the will of the times.
politics.10: Wellspring. The night has a government. When it has to, that government is you.

ride.1: Novice. A quiet horse carries you down the road.
ride.2: Practiced. You stay in the saddle at a trot and keep the rein.
ride.3: Competent. A road, a hunt, and a day's ride are within you.
ride.4: Expert. You ride fast where others dismount.
ride.5: Master. The horse answers a knee, and the chase is your element.
ride.6: Legend. A strange, hot-blooded mount settles under you faster than it throws you.
ride.7: Marvel. Fighting from the saddle is how you arrive, not a circus trick.
ride.8: Myth. You cross ground that should not be crossed mounted.
ride.9: Byword. They say the horse tires later than you do.
ride.10: Absolute. The saddle is another gait. There is almost nowhere for you to fall.

science.1: Student. You know most of what they teach in high school.
science.2: College. You have a decent grasp of the theory.
science.3: Masters. You could teach high school.
science.4: Doctorate. You have the full body of knowledge in your field.
science.5: Scholar. A Nobel Prize is already waiting for you.
science.6: Luminary. Your field cites you where it used to cite the textbook.
science.7: Authority. You can see an experiment that has not been run, and you know how it ends.
science.8: Canon. A theory you corrected becomes what the next students are taught.
science.9: Keeper. The edge of the known is a workplace for you, not a wall.
science.10: Wellspring. Nature in your subject answers as if you had asked in its language.

security.1: Novice. You can pick a simple lock.
security.2: Practiced. You can steal a car.
security.3: Competent. You can walk past a house alarm, or disable it.
security.4: Expert. You can crack a safe.
security.5: Master. You can get a bomb into the Pentagon, or out of it.
security.6: Legend. A lock, an alarm, and a safe are dialects of one craft, and you speak all of them.
security.7: Marvel. You go where a pass will not take you, and you leave with what you came for.
security.8: Myth. A system built against people like you still leaves you a door.
security.9: Byword. A vault people only whisper about is a drawing to you, not a legend.
security.10: Absolute. There is no door that was closed against you personally.

seneschal.1: Novice. You can spend an evening in someone else's house and mix nothing up.
seneschal.2: Practiced. Stores, servants, and the order of the day are within your reach.
seneschal.3: Competent. A small household or court holds while you are watching.
seneschal.4: Expert. You feed them, house them, and keep the place from falling apart in the lord's absence.
seneschal.5: Master. A great court runs as it was meant to, and the guests never notice the work.
seneschal.6: Legend. A strange fortress or a strange staff becomes legible to you in a night.
seneschal.7: Marvel. You see where a house is already stealing from itself.
seneschal.8: Myth. A siege, a feast, and a secret arrival are one list, and it balances.
seneschal.9: Byword. A holding thrives or empties according to whether you hold the keys.
seneschal.10: Absolute. The house is your instrument. Walls, people, and stores do what the night requires.

stealth.1: Novice. You can hide in a dark room.
stealth.2: Practiced. You can move unseen from streetlight to streetlight.
stealth.3: Competent. You have little trouble finding prey in the evening.
stealth.4: Expert. You can move silently across dry leaves.
stealth.6: Legend. You go unnoticed where people are looking straight at the spot: in the light, in a crowd, in someone else's room.
stealth.7: Marvel. You pass a sentry as if you had been struck from his watch.
stealth.8: Myth. Dry leaves, gravel, and a dead silence are equally mute to you.
stealth.9: Byword. Even someone who hunts shadows checks the corner twice, and the corner is still empty.
stealth.10: Absolute. You are absent until you decide that you were seen.

streetwise.1: Novice. You know who sells drugs.
streetwise.2: Practiced. You are respected on the street.
streetwise.3: Competent. You could lead your own gang.
streetwise.4: Expert. You fear little, even in the worst neighborhoods.
streetwise.5: Master. If you have not heard it, it was not said.
streetwise.6: Legend. A strange city becomes gossip to you in a night, not a map.
streetwise.7: Marvel. The underground brings you the rumor itself, so you do not have to ask a rival.
streetwise.8: Myth. If a deal, a raid, or blood happened on the street, you have already been told.
streetwise.9: Byword. Gangs, cops, and the destitute count you as part of the weather.
streetwise.10: Absolute. The street does not say what you are not supposed to hear.

subterfuge.1: Novice. Sometimes you can stretch the truth a little.
subterfuge.5: Master. You are the last person anyone would suspect.
subterfuge.6: Legend. Your lie survives the scrutiny of people who lie for a living.
subterfuge.7: Marvel. You wear someone else's motive so that it looks like your character.
subterfuge.8: Myth. Even the person who has seen through you is not sure that was not what you wanted.
subterfuge.9: Byword. A betrayal from you looks like friendship until the last second.
subterfuge.10: Absolute. The truth about you is one more mask, and it fits better than the rest.

survival.1: Novice. You can survive a five-mile hike.
survival.2: Practiced. You have practiced surviving in rough conditions.
survival.3: Competent. You can tell poisonous mushrooms from edible ones.
survival.4: Expert. You could live for months in the wild if you wanted to.
survival.5: Master. Dropped naked in the Andes, you would still survive.
survival.6: Legend. The wild feeds and hides you as if you were no burden to it.
survival.7: Marvel. You survive where a supplied party is already counting days.
survival.8: Myth. Desert, winter, or mountains are a question of route, not of sentence.
survival.9: Byword. You can be dropped with nothing, and a month later you are fed and not where they looked.
survival.10: Absolute. The world outside the city is home. Hunger and weather call on other people.

theology.1: Novice. You know the prayers and do not confuse a feast with a fast.
theology.2: Practiced. You can argue a point of doctrine without sounding ignorant.
theology.3: Competent. Scripture and rite are working tools for you, not only habit.
theology.4: Expert. Priests listen when you take apart a difficult passage.
theology.5: Master. The faith of the age sits whole in your head: the text, the heresy, and what it does in the square.
theology.6: Luminary. You read a foreign church as surely as your own.
theology.7: Authority. A dispute people were burned over, you can take apart by source and by consequence.
theology.8: Canon. Sacred and forbidden stay distinct for you, even when someone mixed them on purpose.
theology.9: Keeper. You hold a tradition no one is left to serve, and you know which part of it is still dangerous.
theology.10: Wellspring. If a faith has a seam, you can find it and tell what happens if you pull.

strength.5: Outstanding. You can lift 650 lbs. and crush skulls like grapes.
strength.6: Legend. You lift what bends an axle: a car's corner, a gate, a man in armor.
strength.7: Marvel. A door, a beam, a horse — weight is a request, and you decline it.
strength.8: Myth. What was built to hold tears in your hands, and the metal complains before it gives.
strength.9: Byword. They measure you by what is left crooked, not by the pounds.
strength.10: Absolute. Weight holds everyone else. You have already decided otherwise.

dexterity.1: Poor. You are clumsy and awkward. Put that gun down before you hurt yourself.
dexterity.2: Average. You are no oaf, but you are no ballerina.
dexterity.3: Good. You have some athletic potential.
dexterity.4: Exceptional. You could be an acrobat if you wanted.
dexterity.5: Outstanding. Your movements are supple and hypnotic, almost superhuman.
dexterity.6: Legend. A shot, a blade, a hand in a crowd — you are already past the place they aimed.
dexterity.7: Marvel. You cross a room the way other people blink.
dexterity.8: Myth. The weapon finds your hand. You were not looking for it.
dexterity.9: Byword. They say you can take a coin from a sleeping man's eyelid.
dexterity.10: Absolute. The body is already where the thought is only arriving.

stamina.1: Poor. A strong wind can knock you down.
stamina.2: Average. Your health is ordinary, and you can take a blow or two.
stamina.3: Good. You are in good shape and rarely fall ill.
stamina.4: Exceptional. You could run a marathon and perhaps win it, if you wanted.
stamina.5: Outstanding. You have the build of Hercules.
stamina.6: Legend. Hunger, cold, and a night without sleep still leave you standing.
stamina.7: Marvel. What drops a strong man leaves a mark on you, and nothing else.
stamina.8: Myth. You keep going after the body should already have given in.
stamina.9: Byword. They burned you, beat you, and starved you, and the next evening you came back.
stamina.10: Absolute. Pain is news. It is not a decision.

charisma.1: Poor. Stop looking down your nose.
charisma.2: Average. You are generally pleasant, and you have a few friends.
charisma.3: Good. People trust you without reservation.
charisma.4: Exceptional. You have a remarkable personal magnetism.
charisma.5: Outstanding. Whole cultures could follow you.
charisma.6: Legend. A room changes its mind when you finish the sentence.
charisma.7: Marvel. Strangers take your side before they know the argument.
charisma.8: Myth. Hatred sits down when you ask it to.
charisma.9: Byword. A city repeats your name as if it had thought of you itself.
charisma.10: Absolute. They follow. The reason, if it comes, comes after.

manipulation.1: Poor. A person of few, and usually useless, words.
manipulation.2: Average. You can fool people now and then, the same as anyone else.
manipulation.3: Good. You never pay the full price.
manipulation.4: Exceptional. You could be a politician or a cult leader.
manipulation.5: Outstanding. Of course I will tell the prince that I was the one who tried to stake him.
manipulation.6: Legend. You hand a man the knife, and he thanks you for the favor.
manipulation.7: Marvel. The truth you need is the one they offer themselves.
manipulation.8: Myth. Two enemies leave your table sure the third is to blame.
manipulation.9: Byword. A prince signs what you wrote and believes the hand was his.
manipulation.10: Absolute. You do not win the argument. You were never in it. They were.

appearance.1: Poor. You are ugly as mortal sin.
appearance.2: Average. You do not stand out in a crowd, for better or worse.
appearance.3: Good. Strangers often buy you a drink at a bar.
appearance.4: Exceptional. You look good enough to model, and people often tell you so.
appearance.5: Outstanding. People envy you fiercely, or adore you to distraction.
appearance.6: Legend. The sentence is forgotten. The face remains.
appearance.7: Marvel. A crowd parts, and no one can say why they stepped aside.
appearance.8: Myth. Beauty and dread share your features, and both are believed.
appearance.9: Byword. Painters cannot catch you. The sitting outlives the canvas.
appearance.10: Absolute. To look at you is already to have chosen a side.

perception.1: Poor. Maybe you are lost in yourself, or your head is always in the clouds, but either way you miss even the most obvious details.
perception.2: Average. Small details escape you, but you see the picture as a whole.
perception.3: Good. You notice shifts of mood and detail around you.
perception.4: Exceptional. Almost nothing can escape your notice.
perception.5: Outstanding. You see things almost beyond human senses.
perception.6: Legend. You hear the lie in the pause, not in the words.
perception.7: Marvel. A room tells you who left it and what they took.
perception.8: Myth. You notice the thing that was put back.
perception.9: Byword. The night has a seam. You find it with your eyes closed.
perception.10: Absolute. If it happened near you, it did not happen unseen.

intelligence.1: Poor. Your mind is not the sharpest knife in the drawer (IQ 80).
intelligence.2: Average. You are smart enough to know you are the same as everyone else (IQ 100).
intelligence.3: Good. You are smarter than most people (IQ 120).
intelligence.4: Exceptional. Your mind is not merely remarkable. It is brilliant (IQ 140).
intelligence.6: Legend. A problem other people staff a room for, you finish before the cup cools.
intelligence.7: Marvel. A library's argument sits in your head, and you know which page is lying.
intelligence.8: Myth. What was written to hide itself explains itself to you.
intelligence.9: Byword. Scholars come to correct you and leave quoting you.
intelligence.10: Absolute. If the answer exists, it is already late. You have it.

wits.1: Poor. You are easy to dupe.
wits.2: Average. You know when to hold and when to fold in poker.
wits.3: Good. You are rarely surprised or thrown.
wits.4: Exceptional. You are the sort who, the next day, leaves others thinking: Oh, I should have said…
wits.5: Outstanding. You think and answer faster than you can act.
wits.6: Legend. The trap is still speaking, and you are already standing where it is not.
wits.7: Marvel. You answer the question before they finish asking it.
wits.8: Myth. A changing room is still a plan. You are simply already on the new one.
wits.9: Byword. They rehearse what they will say to you. You have already said it.
wits.10: Absolute. Thought and act are the same moment. You are already in it.
